term: modal reading of the tertia via's parameters, and the bridges into the selected relation
definition: modalPossible m w C means C holds at some world accessible from w, and modalIsAt m x v means ExistsAt v x: worlds fill the Time slot of IsNecessary, so x is necessary in this reading exactly when no accessible world is one at which x fails to exist. NecessityCausesAreActualConcreteGrounds m w says that whatever causes the necessity of something other than itself is, at the one reading world w, a concrete individual existing at w that stands in grounds w to it. SimplyPriorIsActualConcreteGround m w says the same of whatever is simply prior to something other than itself. The case's predicates InAct, MoreIn, CausesIn, CausesNecessityOf and PriorSimply have no world index and are read at w.
note: Analyst's vocabulary for #487, with no source. Ordinary meaning: the bridges say that a thing's cause of necessity, and what is simply prior to it, is an existing concrete thing on which it depends in the selected way. Example: in the finite model of AllClausesWitness a concrete individual grounds and is simply prior to another. Counterexamples a rival would give: an abstract law causing the necessity of a concretum, or a form simply prior to its bearer without being a concrete individual (compare DEF-PLOTINIAN-CONSTITUTIVE-NEED); either falsifies the bridge as stated. They differ from STMT-SIMPLY-PRIOR-IS-CAUSE-OF-BEING, which goes from priority to CausesIn and is not used here. No transitivity is assumed; asymmetry and well-foundedness are separate open hypotheses on grounds, and no generalization from experience is offered. A sourced account of grounds (#545) and of Possible would replace the stipulation.
